title: Entropy Production in Mesoscopic Electronic Transport Beyond Weak-Coupling
authors: Ivana R. A. C. Lucena, Caio H. Lewenkopf, Alexandre R. Rocha
abstract: We investigate the full statistics of entropy production in coherent mesoscopic conductors beyond the weak-coupling regime. Using the inside-outside perspective and the Landauer-Büttiker scattering framework, we relate entropy production to the full counting statistics of particle transport and show that the corresponding cumulant-generating function satisfies the fluctuation symmetry independently of the coupling strength. We obtain closed analytical expressions for the cumulant-generating function in the weak- and strong-coupling limits, enabling a detailed characterization of entropy production distributions and higher-order cumulants. These cumulants reveal distinct signatures of resonant transport and coherent fermionic partitioning. While coupling-induced broadening substantially modifies the transport statistics, the fluctuation symmetry imposed by microscopic reversibility remains preserved in the long-time limit.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the statistical fluctuations of entropy production in mesoscopic conductors, moving beyond the simple weak-coupling approximations. By using the full counting statistics framework, the authors demonstrate that the fundamental fluctuation symmetry relating forward and backward entropy production is robustly maintained even when strong coupling and significant level broadening are present. This confirms the deep connection between microscopic reversibility and macroscopic thermodynamic constraints in quantum transport.
main_problem: The paper investigates the full statistics of entropy production in coherent mesoscopic electronic transport, specifically extending the analysis beyond the standard weak-coupling regime.
main_result: The fluctuation symmetry governing entropy production remains strictly preserved in the steady-state, long-time limit, even when substantial coherent broadening modifies the transport statistics.
method: The analysis employs the Landauer-Büttiker scattering framework, relating entropy production to the full counting statistics (FCS) of particle transport via the Cumulant Generating Function (CGF).
model_or_system: The model is a two-terminal mesoscopic conductor connected to electronic reservoirs, analyzed in regimes ranging from weak-coupling (isolated resonances) to strong-coupling (broadened resonances).
key_observables: Entropy production ($\sigma$), particle transfer full counting statistics, and higher-order cumulants ($S(\infty), K(\infty)$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($\Gamma$), bias voltage ($\Delta\mu$), temperature ($T$), and channel transparency ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes isothermal conditions ($T_L = T_R = T$) and relies on extending theoretical results derived initially for weak coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the difference between weak-coupling and strong-coupling resonance regimes, and show the bias dependence of particle transfer probabilities and the behavior of the first four cumulants as a function of channel transparency.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general framework of FCS and entropy production, derives analytical expressions for the CGF in different limits, and then analyzes how higher-order cumulants reveal distinct signatures of resonant transport while confirming the robustness of the fluctuation symmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous extension of fluctuation theorems into the strongly coupled, non-equilibrium regime of quantum transport, which is crucial for understanding irreversible processes in nanoscale devices.
